definition: Generating sequences of human motion — skeleton poses or full video — conditioned on action labels or text descriptions.
details: Generating sequences of human motion — skeleton poses or full video — conditioned on action labels or text descriptions.

explainer.lead: Human action generation is the task of generating sequences of human motion — skeleton poses or full video — conditioned on action labels or text descriptions. It matters for producing realistic, controllable human movement in animation and simulation.

tiers.eli5: You tell a computer 'jumping jack' or 'walking,' and it draws or animates a person doing exactly that movement.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers condition motion generators on class labels or text prompts to synthesise poses or video for animation and data augmentation. A pitfall is that generated motion can look plausible frame by frame but drift or lose physical consistency over long sequences.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally stated as generating sequences of human motion, either skeleton poses or full video, conditioned on action labels or text descriptions; the given facts specify no metrics or limits.

explainer.example: Given the text prompt 'a person waving,' a model outputs a skeleton pose sequence of a waving arm for use in an animated character.
